newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ICICI, SCICI boards approve merger.
newsitem.headline: India's ICICI, SCICI boards approve merger.

text.p: The boards of Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Ltd (ICICI) and SCICI on Tuesday approved a proposal to merge the two institutions, an ICICI statement said.
It said the merger would be effective April 1, 1996.
The swap ratio would be two shares of ICICI for every five of SCICI, the statement said.
"The equity share exchange ratio for the proposed merger has been decided as two equity shares of ICICI of face value ten rupees each for every five shares of SCICI of face value ten rupees each."
The merger would be subject to the completion of legal formalities, ICICI said.
"The merger is subject to necessary approvals and due confirmation of the Scheme of Amalgamation by the Bombay High Court."
The statement said the proposed merger would obviate duplication of efforts in lending and raising of resources as both institutions had common clients and investors, both international and domestic.
The merger was required as size had become a critical factor in the emerging scenario of increasing competition in the financial sectors, it said.

"The experience over the last 18 months has underscored the need for large players in the Indian financial markets. With increasing competition and challenges from large domestic as well as international players in the financial sector, the critical success factor would be size, in respect of both lending and resources raising activities."
The merger would enable the new entity to take on exposures in projects which are increasingly on an international scale, particularly in the infrastructure sector, ICICI said.
"A single large entity would be well poised to assume a leading role in financing of new roads and ports and power and telecommunications projects."
The merger would create an institution with a net worth of about 40 billion rupees and an asset base of more than 330 billion, the statement said.

The merged entity would have a capital adequacy of over 13 percent. Non-performing assets would be around six percent of the total loan portfolio, one of the lowest in the Indian financial sector, the statement added.
